report.summary: Audit of bus.py reveals a cross-process concurrency flaw breaking hash chain integrity, missing identity-field scan for secret floor anonymous receipts, and anchor/transcript inconsistency after crashes. Docstring guarantees around refusal receipt degradation are not implemented.

risks.description: Cross-process concurrent appends corrupt hash chain: multiple processes can read same tail state and write conflicting chain links with same 'prev', breaking integrity. Trigger: two Python processes run append_round simultaneously on same council store. _WRITE_LOCK is only thread-local, not inter-process.
risks.location: bus.py: _chain_state and _chain_records (visible portion), no inter-process file lock.

risks.description: Docstring claims refusal receipt degrades to anonymous when identity fields carry a secret, but _scan_turn returns only a rule label with no information about which field triggered the floor. The caller cannot detect identity-field hits, so anonymous fallback never occurs. Trigger: turn with secret in actor field passes through _scan_turn; receipt still includes sensitive identity.
risks.location: bus.py: _scan_turn returns str | None; _refusal_receipt requires explicit anonymous flag.

risks.description: Anchor file not written atomically nor protected by transaction with transcript. Crash during anchor write can leave old count, causing verification failures. Trigger: system crash between append and anchor update.
risks.location: bus.py: _write_anchor writes directly; no atomic rename or sync with chain state.

risks.description: No re-scan of refusal receipt content to ensure no residual secret; anchor record might still leak. Guarantee not met.

todos: Add inter-process file locking (e.g., fcntl/msvcrt) around chain appends and anchor updates.
Modify _scan_turn to return hit location (e.g., field name) so refusal can degrade to anonymous for identity hits.
Re-scan refusal receipt record with secret_floor_rule before writing to ensure no leaks.
Implement atomic anchor update (write to temp and rename).

handoff.suggestion: Review the chain append logic for cross-process safety. The threading lock is insufficient for multi-process writers. Consider using a file lock or pipe-based queue. Also, the anonymous refusal mechanism is not implemented in the scanning layer; it needs to distinguish identity-field hits.
